results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response: The major subdivisions of the Drosophila [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. This information comes from the Virtual Fly Brain database.

results.title: Neuron type classification
results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?
results.response: The adult Drosophila brain contains multiple types of Kenyon cells. VFB records show several types, including [KCab-c(i)](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049111 "Open [KCab-c](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00110929 "Open KCab-c in Virtual Fly Brain")(i) in Virtual Fly Brain"), KCab-c, [KCg-m](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111061 "Open KCg-m in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Kenyon cell of main calyx](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047926 "Open [Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain") of main calyx in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [gamma Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100247 "Open gamma Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"). Additionally, VFB indicates that Kenyon cells can be classified into alpha/beta, alpha'/beta', and gamma Kenyon cells, which are further subdivided into subtypes such as core, surface, posterior, anterior-posterior, middle, dorsal, and main classes. VFB holds [37](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of Kenyon cell") subclasses of Kenyon cell.

results.title: Central complex structure
results.question: What are the main components of the Drosophila central complex and what functions are they associated with?
results.response: The main components of the central complex include the ellipsoid body, the fan-shaped body, the paired noduli, the asymmetrical bodies, and the protocerebral bridge. These components are associated with functions such as navigation/orientation, locomotor control, and sleep/arousal or memory-related behaviours, as indicated by the connectome data and functional literature. VFB records show these components as part of the adult central complex description.

results.title: Neuron characterisation
results.question: What is known about the LPLC2 visual neuron type? Where is it, what does it connect to, and what is its function?
results.response: The [lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111763 "Open lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2 in Virtual Fly Brain") is located in the dorsal area of the lateral cell body rind and has distinct dendritic arbors in each lobula plate layer. This arrangement allows it to detect looming stimuli, which elicits a jump escape response. The LPLC2 projects to an optic glomerulus of the PVLP, anterior to LPLC1 and dorsal to LC4, and has presynaptic sites in layer 4 of the lobula. VFB records show that there are approximately 80 of these cells per optic lobe, and they are cholinergic. The connectome data indicates that LPLC2 has connections that allow it to play a role in detecting looming stimuli and initiating a jump escape response. VFB does not currently hold detailed data on the specific postsynaptic targets of LPLC2.

results.response: The organisation of the [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") compares between adult and larval Drosophila in terms of glomerular organization. According to VFB, the adult antennal lobe has approximately 50 glomeruli, while the larval antennal lobe has around 22 glomeruli. results.title: Anatomical containment chain

results.response: The anatomical containment hierarchy from the DA1 glomerulus up to the top-level brain structure is: DA1 glomerulus -> adult olfactory antennal lobe glomerulus -> adult antennal lobe -> adult deutocerebrum -> adult cerebrum -> adult central brain -> adult brain. This information comes from VFB, as recorded in the trace containment chain. Each level in the hierarchy represents a brain structure that anatomically contains the previous one.

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior, as stated by Thomas and Wyman (1984). It is a [primary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047097 "Open primary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), according to Allen et al. (1998), Dorkenwald et al. (2024), and Schlegel et al. (2024). 

VFB records show the giant fiber neuron has connectivity with various neuron types, including [adult VNC neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00059289 "Open adult VNC neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [thoracic neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00001983 "Open thoracic neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [secondary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047096 "Open secondary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Notch OFF hemilineage neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049540 "Open Notch OFF hemilineage neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [mesothoracic neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00001985 "Open mesothoracic neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), primary neuron, [Notch OFF hemilineage secondary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049542 "Open Notch OFF hemilineage secondary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [prothoracic neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00001984 "Open prothoracic neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Notch ON hemilineage neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049539 "Open Notch ON hemilineage neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [NB2-4 lineage neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00048927 "Open NB2-4 lineage neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Notch ON hemilineage secondary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049541 "Open Notch ON hemilineage secondary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [input/output neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00053396 "Open input/output neuron in Virtual Fly Brain").

For a comprehensive profile, including available driver lines and relevant publications, the user can query VFB directly. VFB does not currently hold data on specific driver lines for the giant fiber neuron. Relevant publications include those by Thomas and Wyman (1984), Allen et al. (1998), Dorkenwald et al. (2024), and Schlegel et al. (2024).

results.title: Concepts: NBLAST
results.question: What is NBLAST and what does an NBLAST similarity score mean?
results.response: NBLAST is a method to quantify morphological similarity. The final NBLAST score is the sum over all query-target vector pairs, typically normalized to a self-self comparison, where a perfect match would be 1. This means that an NBLAST similarity score represents how similar the morphology of one neuron is to another, with a score of 1 indicating a perfect match. NBLAST is computed per registered neuron, allowing for a scored comparison of individual neurons. The evidence does not provide specific details on the number of registered neurons or the nearest neighbors for a particular query.

results.title: API: REST endpoints
results.question: How can I query Virtual Fly Brain programmatically using the SOLR or Owlery API?
results.response: The Virtual Fly Brain can be queried programmatically using the SOLR or Owlery API. The Owlery API provides OWL reasoning services for Virtual Fly Brain's ontologies, enabling complex queries over class hierarchies and relationships. The SOLR Search API provides fast text search and autocomplete functionality for Virtual Fly Brain entities, datasets, and publications. For more information on using the Owlery API, see the Virtual Fly Brain documentation at https://www.virtualflybrain.org/docs/apis/owlery.

results.title: API: integrations
results.question: How do I explore Virtual Fly Brain neurons using Navis or pymaid?
results.response: To explore Virtual Fly Brain neurons, you can use the tutorials provided on the Virtual Fly Brain website. Specifically, for exploring neurons using navis, you can load an example neuron and access its properties, such as its ID, root node, and node table, as shown in the example code `n = navis.example_neurons(1, kind='skeleton')`. However, the provided evidence does not specify how to use pymaid for this purpose.

results.title: Anatomy teaching diagrams
results.question: Is there a circuit diagram of the mushroom body available on Virtual Fly Brain?
results.response: There is a schematic representation of the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") available on Virtual Fly Brain, which shows the compartmental organisation of the [adult mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003684 "Open adult mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") lobes. This includes how the dendrites of mushroom body output neurons and the axon terminals of dopaminergic neurons tile the lobes into a stereotyped grid of 15 compartments.
